settings.name: metaverse
settings.label: Connection
settings.description: How this server connects your world to Darkride, and how visitors reach it.

settings.name: access_token
settings.label: Access token
settings.help: Links this server to your Darkride account. The Connect button above fills it in; you can also make one on your account's page at vr.darkride.ai and paste it here.

settings.name: id
settings.label: World ID
settings.help: Which of your Darkride worlds this server is.

settings.name: automatic_networking
settings.label: How visitors reach this server
settings.help: Leave this on Automatic unless you know you need something else: Darkride then finds a way through your router for visitors by itself.

options.label: Automatic: Darkride finds a way through your router (recommended)
My address only: I've opened the server's port on my router myself
Manual: use only the network details I've entered

settings.name: local_port
settings.label: Local UDP port
settings.help: The network port this server listens on. Running several servers on one network may need each to have its own; 0 lets the server pick a free one.

settings.name: enable_packet_verification
settings.label: Check every packet
settings.help: Adds a checksum to the server's network traffic, for extra security at a small cost in speed.

settings.label: Arrival points
settings.description: Named spots in your world that visitors can go straight to, and where they arrive when they don't name one.

settings.name: paths
settings.label: Arrival points
settings.help: Visitors can add a path to your world's address to arrive at a particular spot. Each row maps a path to where they appear. The path / is where everyone arrives when they don't name one.

settings.name: descriptors
settings.label: World listing
settings.description: How your world is described where people look for worlds to visit.
settings.help: This data will be queryable from your server. It may be collected by Darkride and used to share your world with others.

settings.name: description
settings.label: Description
settings.help: A sentence or two about your world (up to 256 characters).

settings.name: maturity
settings.label: Maturity rating
settings.help: A guide to who your world's content suits.

settings.name: hosts
settings.label: Hosts
settings.help: Usernames of people who can welcome new visitors and show them around.

settings.name: tags
settings.label: Tags
settings.help: Words for the kinds of world yours is, to help people find it.

settings.name: security
settings.label: Access and permissions
settings.description: Who can sign in to these pages, how many visitors can come in, and what each kind of visitor may do.

settings.name: http_username
settings.label: Admin username
settings.help: The username these pages ask for.

settings.name: http_password
settings.label: Admin password
settings.help: The password these pages ask for.

settings.name: verify_http_password
settings.label: Admin password again
settings.help: The password again, to check it.

settings.name: maximum_user_capacity
settings.label: Most visitors at once
settings.help: How many people can be in your world at the same time; 0 for no limit. Several avatars from the same computer count as one.

settings.name: maximum_user_capacity_redirect_location
settings.label: When it's full, send visitors to
settings.help: An address to send people to when your world is full, such as another world. Empty, they're told it's full.

settings.name: ac_subnet_whitelist
settings.label: Script runners allowed from
settings.help: The addresses of other computers allowed to run this world's servers and scripts (its assignment clients): one IP address, or a range such as 10.0.0.0/24. This computer is always allowed.

settings.name: standard_permissions
settings.label: Everyone, by kind of visitor
settings.section_help: Tick what each kind of visitor may do here. The tables after this one give particular groups, people or computers more, or less.
settings.help: Tick what each kind of visitor may do: anonymous is anyone not signed in, logged-in anyone signed in to Darkride, friends your Darkride friends, and localhost anyone on this computer. What do these mean?

groups.label: What they may do ?

settings.name: group_permissions
settings.help: Give the members of a Darkride group, or one rank of them, their own permissions.
settings.caption: Members of a group
settings.new_category_message: Save and reload to see ranks

groups.label: What they may do ?

settings.name: group_forbiddens
settings.help: Take permissions away from a group's members, even where another row gives them.
settings.caption: Taken away from members of a group
settings.new_category_message: Save and reload to see ranks

groups.label: What they may do ?

settings.name: permissions
settings.help: Permissions for named Darkride users.
settings.caption: Particular people

groups.label: What they may do ?

settings.name: ip_permissions
settings.help: Permissions for anyone connecting from a given IP address.
settings.caption: Visitors from an IP address

groups.label: What they may do ?

settings.name: mac_permissions
settings.help: Permissions for anyone connecting from a computer with a given network card (MAC address).
settings.caption: Visitors from a network card

groups.label: What they may do ?

settings.name: machine_fingerprint_permissions
settings.help: Permissions for anyone connecting from a given computer (its machine fingerprint).
settings.caption: Visitors from a particular computer

groups.label: What they may do ?

settings.name: multi_kick_logged_in
settings.label: Removing a signed-in visitor removes their computer too
settings.help: When you remove someone who is signed in, also keep out their computer (by its fingerprint), not only their username.

settings.name: scripts
settings.label: Always-running scripts
settings.description: Scripts the server keeps running in your world, whether or not anyone is there.

settings.name: persistent_scripts
settings.label: Always-running scripts
settings.help: The address of each script to keep running, how many copies of it to run, and (optionally) which group of script runners runs it.

settings.name: audio_threading
settings.label: Audio processing
settings.description: How much of the computer the sound mixing may use.

settings.name: auto_threads
settings.label: Choose the number of threads automatically
settings.help: Recommended.

settings.name: num_threads
settings.label: Number of threads
settings.help: How many threads mix sound, when not chosen automatically.

settings.name: throttle_start
settings.label: Start easing off at
settings.help: The share of each frame's time, from 0 to 1, at which mixing starts doing less to keep up.

settings.name: throttle_backoff
settings.label: Stop easing off at
settings.help: The share of each frame's time, from 0 to 1, below which mixing goes back to normal.

settings.name: audio_env
settings.label: Sound
settings.description: How voices and sounds carry around your world, and the echo of its rooms.

settings.name: attenuation_per_doubling_in_distance
settings.label: How quickly sound fades with distance
settings.help: From 0 (sound never fades) to 1 (it fades very fast). 0.5 suits most worlds.

settings.name: noise_muting_threshold
settings.label: Mute background noise below
settings.help: From 0 (mutes everyone) to 1 (never mutes). Around 0.003 mutes most background noise.

settings.name: enable_filter
settings.label: Soften distant sounds
settings.help: Muffles sounds a little with distance, as real air does.

settings.name: zones
settings.label: Sound zones
settings.help: Boxes in your world that can have their own fading and echo, below. Each is a name and its corners, in metres.

settings.name: attenuation_coefficients
settings.label: Fading between zones
settings.help: How quickly sound fades from one zone to another, where it differs from the world's.

settings.name: reverb
settings.label: Echo
settings.help: Echo for a zone. A meeting room of about 100 m² suits a decay of about 1.5 seconds and a 25% mix; a hall or cathedral, 4 seconds and 50%.

settings.name: codec_preference_order
settings.label: Audio codecs, best first
settings.help: The sound formats the server prefers, in order, by name.

settings.name: audio_buffer
settings.label: Audio buffering
settings.description: How the server smooths out sound that arrives unevenly over the network.

settings.name: dynamic_jitter_buffer
settings.label: Adjust buffering automatically
settings.help: Buffers incoming sound by how unevenly it arrives. Recommended.

settings.name: static_desired_jitter_buffer_frames
settings.label: Fixed buffer size (frames)
settings.help: When buffering isn't automatic, how much sound to buffer. More smooths it better but adds delay.

settings.name: avatars
settings.label: Avatars
settings.description: Limits on the avatars visitors wear in your world.

settings.name: min_avatar_height
settings.label: Shortest avatar (metres)
settings.help: No avatar can be shorter than this. At least 0.009.

settings.name: max_avatar_height
settings.label: Tallest avatar (metres)
settings.help: No avatar can be taller than this. At most 1755.

settings.name: avatar_whitelist
settings.label: Avatars allowed only from
settings.help: Web addresses (separated by commas, paths allowed) that avatars must come from. An avatar from anywhere else is swapped for the replacement below. Empty, any avatar is allowed.

settings.name: replacement_avatar
settings.label: Replacement avatar
settings.help: The address of the avatar (.fst) worn instead of one that isn't allowed. Empty, the default avatar.

settings.name: avatar_mixer
settings.label: Avatar traffic
settings.description: How the server shares visitors' avatars with each other over the network.

settings.name: max_node_send_bandwidth
settings.label: Bandwidth to each visitor (Mbit/s)
settings.help: The most avatar data sent to each visitor each second.

settings.name: auto_threads
settings.label: Choose the number of threads automatically
settings.help: Recommended.

settings.name: num_threads
settings.label: Number of threads
settings.help: How many threads share avatars, when not chosen automatically.

settings.name: connection_rate
settings.label: New visitors each second
settings.help: How many visitors can join the avatar mixer each second.

settings.name: priority_fraction
settings.label: Share kept for "hero" zones
settings.help: The share of bandwidth, from 0 to 1, kept for avatars in zones marked as hero zones.

settings.name: entity_server_settings
settings.label: World objects
settings.description: How the server stores, saves, backs up and checks the objects your world is made of (its entities).

settings.name: maxTmpLifetime
settings.label: Longest life of a temporary object (seconds)
settings.help: An object set to disappear after this many seconds or fewer counts as temporary.

settings.name: dynamicDomainVerificationTimeMin
settings.label: Ownership checks, at the soonest (seconds)
settings.help: The shortest time before the server re-checks who owns certified objects.

settings.name: dynamicDomainVerificationTimeMax
settings.label: Ownership checks, at the latest (seconds)
settings.help: The longest time before the server re-checks who owns certified objects.

settings.name: entityScriptSourceWhitelist
settings.label: Object scripts allowed only from
settings.help: Web addresses (separated by commas, paths allowed) that objects' scripts must come from. A script from anywhere else is refused. Empty, scripts from anywhere are allowed.

settings.name: entityEditFilter
settings.label: Edit filter script
settings.help: A script that checks every change to an object, and can refuse or alter it.
settings.placeholder: url whose content is like: function filter(properties) { return properties; }

settings.name: persistFilePath
settings.label: Where the world is saved
settings.help: The file the world's objects are saved in, ending .json.gz. A relative path is in the server's data folder.

settings.name: backupDirectoryPath
settings.label: Where backups go
settings.help: The folder for backups. A relative path is in the server's data folder.

settings.name: persistInterval
settings.label: Check for changes to save every (milliseconds)
settings.help: How often the server looks for changes to save.

settings.name: NoPersist
settings.label: Don't save the world
settings.help: Changes are lost when the server stops.

settings.name: NoBackup
settings.label: Don't back the world up
settings.help: Turns off the regular backups of the saved world.

settings.name: statusHost
settings.label: Status page host
settings.help: The host name or IP address for the entity server's status page.

settings.name: statusPort
settings.label: Status page port
settings.help: The port for the entity server's status page.

settings.name: persistFileDownload
settings.label: Offer the saved world for download
settings.help: Adds a link to download the saved world on the status page.

settings.name: wantEditLogging
settings.label: Log every edit
settings.section_help: For tracking down problems: these fill the log quickly.
settings.help: Writes every change to an object to the log.

settings.name: wantTerseEditLogging
settings.label: Log every edit, briefly
settings.help: Writes a short line for every change to an object.

settings.name: verboseDebug
settings.label: Verbose debugging
settings.help: A great deal of detail in the log.

settings.name: debugReceiving
settings.label: Debug what's received
settings.help: Extra detail about incoming data.

settings.name: debugSending
settings.label: Debug what's sent
settings.help: Extra detail about outgoing data.

settings.name: debugTimestampNow
settings.label: Debug timestamps
settings.help: Extra detail about the server's clock.

settings.name: clockSkew
settings.label: Clock skew (milliseconds)
settings.help: Moves the server's clock, to test how clients cope.

settings.name: asset_server
settings.label: File storage
settings.description: The server's own store for the files your world uses (its asset server, at atp: addresses).

settings.name: enabled
settings.label: Run the file store
settings.help: Serves your world's files to visitors from this server, at atp: addresses.

settings.name: assets_path
settings.label: Where the files are kept
settings.help: The folder for the stored files. A relative path is in the server's data folder. If you change it, move the files there yourself.

settings.name: assets_filesize_limit
settings.label: Largest file (MB)
settings.help: The biggest file anyone can add; 0 for no limit.

settings.name: physics_server
settings.label: Vehicle physics
settings.description: A server that moves your world's vehicles, so every visitor sees them in the same place.

settings.name: enabled
settings.label: Run vehicle physics on the server
settings.help: For worlds with vehicles (trains on Track entities, driven cars, airships): the server moves them, so every visitor sees the same vehicle in the same place. Off, each vehicle is moved by one visitor's Darkride, which works but is less steady. Off costs nothing; on, it takes up to about a tenth of one CPU core, even while nothing moves. Saving this restarts your world server.

settings.name: entity_script_server
settings.label: Server scripts
settings.description: Limits on the scripts that run on the server for your world's objects.

settings.name: entity_pps_per_script
settings.label: Updates each script may send each second
settings.help: How many updates each server script may send to the world's objects each second. They add up to a total all scripts share: 1000 each for 5 scripts is 5000, of which one script could use 4000.

settings.name: max_total_entity_pps
settings.label: Most updates from all scripts each second
settings.help: A cap on the total above: with 5 scripts at 1000 each, a cap of 4000 keeps them to 4000 together.

settings.name: broadcasting
settings.label: Sharing between servers
settings.description: Passing avatars between linked world servers, for very large events.

settings.name: users
settings.label: Avatars to share
settings.help: The users whose avatars are sent on to the receiving servers.

settings.name: downstream_servers
settings.label: Servers that receive them
settings.help: Servers this one sends the shared avatars to.

settings.name: upstream_servers
settings.label: Servers that send to this one
settings.help: Servers that share their avatars with this one.

settings.name: oauth
settings.label: Admin sign-in with an account
settings.description: Let chosen Darkride accounts manage this server, signing in to these pages with their account instead of the admin password.

settings.name: admin-users
settings.label: Accounts that can manage this server
settings.help: Any of these Darkride users can sign in to these pages.

settings.name: admin-roles
settings.label: Roles that can manage this server
settings.help: Any Darkride user with one of these roles can sign in to these pages.

settings.name: client-id
settings.label: Client ID
settings.help: The ID this server signs in to the account service with.

settings.name: client-secret
settings.label: Client secret
settings.help: The secret that goes with the client ID.

settings.name: provider
settings.label: Account service
settings.help: The address of the account service people sign in with.

settings.name: hostname
settings.label: This server's address
settings.help: The host name these pages are reached at.

settings.name: key-passphrase
settings.label: Certificate key passphrase
settings.help: The passphrase for the HTTPS certificate's private key.

settings.name: automatic_content_archives
settings.label: Automatic backups
settings.description: How often the server backs up your world's content, and how many backups it keeps.

settings.name: backup_rules
settings.label: Backup schedule
settings.help: Each row is a backup that's made over and over: how often, and how many to keep before the oldest goes.

columns.name: backupInterval
columns.label: Every (seconds)
columns.help: How often this backup is made, in seconds: 3600 is an hour, 86400 a day.

columns.name: maxBackupVersions
columns.label: Keep this many
columns.help: How many of these backups to keep; the oldest goes when there are more.
